doc.title: Arthur Davis and Andy Mosley Interview, 1960-01-12

title: Remembering a fellow inmate who died in 1959
summary: A speaker remembers a young inmate who helped the prison and died at Camp A on August 11, 1959, before Oster's expected return; he was 35.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: He died now. Yes, sir. He was a very swell fellow. He was always practically wanting to participate in anything that the other inmates would do beneficial to the prison. In August 11, 59, before they went on and taken with Q and Justin and died in one of the units over at Camp A. You know, he was waiting for a return in September from Mr. Austin. He was supposed to come back. He was on a tour. So, Mr. Austin, the professor, used to come up here. And he would say he was going to make some more records and let them know how he was doing. And he was on his tour during the time he was on his vacation. But he was supposed to come back in September. But it happened to be unfortunate that a fellow passed away August 11, 1949. Roger and the mates.
Now, you say he was quite young?

Yes, sir. His age was 35, which is why I've been familiar with his age. We gave him a birthday party over at Camp A when I was living quarters over there before I got transferred back here last year in 49.
